thread:
julie: FYI there's a P0 from ACME support — their app started getting 503s from our text-generation API around 10:12 UTC. They say it used to be 429s. :rotating_light:
alex: link to support ticket?
julie: https://support.example.com/t/ACME-451 (copied errors below). They pasted a curl response: `HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable\n{\"error\":\"quota service failure\"}`
sam: that's the symptom we see when quota-orch times out talking to rate-db, but usually we convert that to 429. did something change in fallback mapping?
maria: checking logs for quota-orch now. grabbing tail:```
[2026-03-15T10:11:45Z] quota-orch request id=abc123 user=acme token=tok_XXXX route=/v1/generate
[2026-03-15T10:11:45Z] upstream auth-cache lookup start
[2026-03-15T10:11:48Z] auth-cache request timeout after 3s
[2026-03-15T10:11:48Z] quota-orch failed to get limit: upstream timeout error
[2026-03-15T10:11:48Z] quota-orch returning 500 to gateway (code=upstream_timeout)
```
alex: aha, `quota-orch returning 500` — our proxy layer should map `upstream_timeout` to a 429 client-facing, but looks like a regression. who pushed quota-orch last 24h?
julie: customer says it started ~10:06. can we patch quickly — customer on a paid Dedicated plan, they're impacted.
oncall-sre: paging oncall. @alex @sam are oncall?
oncall-sre: auto-escalation sent to oncall-sre (channel). deploy-bot: started rollout `quota-orch@2026.03.15-rc3` at 09:58 UTC
sam: that rollout had a refactor to error handling (PR #594). I wonder if we dropped the `translate_timeout_to_429` code path. pulling PR now.
maria: current observation: quota-orch is timing out on our auth-cache due to increased latencies from the new config on auth-cache (cache warming spike). when auth-cache times out it raises an upstream timeout exception that now propagates as 500 instead of being intercepted.
alex: we need a mitigation: 1) temporary route change to force fallback 429 behavior at gateway, or 2) hotfix in quota-orch to map that exception to a 429. which is faster?
sam: quick mitigation: we can flip gateway config `translate-upstream-timeouts-to-429=true` globally for the hosted API. that avoids deploy. I'll open a PR to change the runtime flag in gateway-config and apply to edge cluster.
oncall-sre: do it but careful with non-deliberate behavior for other clients. limit to hosted inference region prod-us-east-1 first.
julie: ACME wants ETA. can we tell them 20-30m?
alex: yes if runtime change applies fast. sam do you have steps?
sam: steps: `kubectl patch cm gateway-config -n prod --patch '{\"data\":{\"translate-upstream-timeouts-to-429\":\"true\"}}'` then restart gateway pods with `rollout restart deploy/gateway -n prod`. I'll apply to us-east first. Note: this will map `upstream_timeout` and `upstream_unavailable` to 429.
maria: I'm also reverting the auth-cache config change to reduce timeout spikes (rollback config map `auth-cache-config` to previous). that should reduce timeouts.
deploy-bot: applied patch to configmap `gateway-config` in `prod-us-east-1` at 10:24 UTC, rollout started (5 pods).
alex: monitoring error rates and 5xx -> 429 conversion. set alert to track 5xx count for `/v1/generate`.
oncall-sre: added Grafana panel with filter `service:gateway status:5xx` and slack alert to #incidents.
maria: auth-cache revert rolled out at 10:28 (2m ago). CPU and latency trending down.
sam: gateway pods back up, translation flag active. I can see calls returning 429 now in logs for previously impacted tokens:```
[2026-03-15T10:29:03Z] gateway request id=abc123 translated upstream_timeout -> 429 for client acme
[2026-03-15T10:29:03Z] response HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests {retry_after:30s}
```
julie: customer confirms they now see 429s instead of 503s, their app resumed normal backoff. they still saw some failed jobs during the window. asking for RCA and compensation.
alex: next steps: 1) postmortem with timeline and root cause (auth-cache config caused a latency spike; quota-orch error handling regression in PR #594 allowed 500 to surface), 2) revert the PR on quota-orch to restore mapping and add unit test, 3) add integration test in gateway to assert translation of upstream timeouts, 4) run chaos test for auth-cache latency to ensure graceful degradation, 5) customer engagement + credits.
sam: I already opened follow-up PRs: #601 (revert error handling), #602 (add unit test). will mark for immediate cherry-pick to prod.
oncall-sre: continuing to watch. lowering alert severity now that rates are back to baseline but leaving monitoring for 2h.
julie: thanks team — I'll draft a support update and start compensation workflow for ACME. posting rough timeline to ticket. :heart:
alex: assigning postmortem owner @sam. please include the config diff for auth-cache and the exact commit that introduced regression.
sam: on it. I'll collect logs and push a short incident writeup once PRs land.
maria: note for follow-up: increase auth-cache autoscaling threshold and add a health endpoint to avoid hanging requests.
julie: closing this slack thread after we publish RCA. updating support ticket and pinging customer.
